name: Rismorelin
lead: Rismorelin is a synthetic peptide in the growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) analog family, the group of compounds that prompt the pituitary gland to release the body's own growth hormone. People interested in physique and recovery follow this family because growth hormone signalling is associated with lean mass, fat distribution and tissue repair, which feed into how a physique looks.[1][2]

Rismorelin appears in lists of GHRH receptor agonists alongside sermorelin, the 29-amino-acid GHRH fragment, and tesamorelin; Wikipedia's articles on those compounds mention rismorelin only in a navigation template, without description.[1][2][1] Published human data on rismorelin itself were not found, and its public footprint is much smaller than that of sermorelin or tesamorelin.

GHRH itself is a 44-amino-acid hypothalamic peptide that acts on the pituitary GHRH receptor, and its release and the resulting growth hormone release are pulsatile.[2] Wikipedia says most GHRH analogues remain research chemicals and may be restricted for professional athletes under anti-doping rules because they act as growth hormone secretagogues.[2]

chain: Binds the GHRH receptor on the pituitary
Prompts pulses of the body's own growth hormone
Growth hormone signalling is linked to lean mass and body composition
angle.text: People who use GHRH analogs aim to raise growth hormone release to support leaner body composition and recovery from training. Rismorelin belongs to this group, though it is discussed far less than its relatives.

infobox: Not marketed as an approved product

paras: GHRH analogs bind the GHRH receptor, a G protein-coupled receptor on pituitary somatotroph cells, which raises cAMP and drives growth hormone gene transcription and release.[2] Release is pulsatile because somatostatin opposes GHRH and the two alternate; for sermorelin, the same negative feedback is said to limit the response.[2][1]

Sermorelin was approved by the FDA in 1997 as Geref, used mainly to test growth hormone secretion and in children with growth hormone deficiency, and its manufacturer discontinued it in 2008 for commercial reasons; it can still be obtained through compounding pharmacies.[1] Tesamorelin (Egrifta) received FDA approval in 2010 for HIV-associated lipodystrophy.[2]

Rismorelin does not have a dedicated Wikipedia article and is far less discussed in training and looksmaxxing communities than sermorelin.[1] No forum or news discussion of rismorelin specifically was found.

card.summary: A GHRH-analog peptide in the family used to prompt the body's own growth hormone release for leaner body composition and recovery.
card.note: Very little published information is available on rismorelin specifically.

quick.overview:
Rismorelin is a growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) analog, a peptide that signals the pituitary to release growth hormone.

People interested in physique follow this class because growth hormone is associated with lean mass and recovery. Rismorelin itself is much less documented than relatives such as sermorelin.
quick.mechanism: It is classed as a GHRH receptor agonist: it binds the GHRH receptor on the pituitary and prompts growth hormone release, which for related compounds occurs in pulses limited by somatostatin feedback.
quick.risks: Little specific safety information is published for rismorelin. It is not a marketed approved product, and related GHRH peptides are available mainly through prescription or compounding channels.
